chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: Year 1218. Pysahiax emptied.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 1218. Sickness in Volu. Wolves were seen near Brerdrom.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 1218. Pestilence at Tholaevol. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1218, a great fire broke out in Breskind and the watchtower was lost. The bells were recast.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1220. Tailed star above the noon road, milky, 4 nights.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: In the year 1226, the wells of Grouka ran dry.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1226, no rain fell in Pexiarwyth from spring to autumn.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1229. Pilgrims at Grouka (called Breskind by others).

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 1230. Comet above the morning sea, snowy. 12 nights.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 1233, the Breitugask forgot its bed and wandered over Pexiarwyth (called Volu by others), drowning the sheaves.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 1235, King Krokax took a wife from Riamur.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: Year 1235. Red moon over Draeziatam. Wolves were seen near Briagri.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 1247. Battle at Briagri with Wosel; King Krokax lost many men.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1247, King Krokax fought the men of Ideives at Riamur and won the field. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1248. Fire at Sazouv (called Keba by others).

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1251. New star over the dawn ridge, 4 weeks.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1253, King Byrarn fought the men of Ideives at Brerdrom and won the field. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Pysahiax
text: 1254. Bearded light towards the setting sun. pale. 5 nights.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 1254. Comet over the evening hills, ash-coloured. 5 nights.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 1260 of the Reckoning, the bread of Draeziatam ran out, and men fought over a sack of bran.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1266. Earthen swarm. Volu (called Pexiarwyth by others) stripped.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1279, the winter was hard and the Thatham froze from bank to bank.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1280. Hunger at Tholaevol.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1280, a pestilence came to Draeziatam and many died.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: That year, 1281, the coughing sickness spread through Sonobun (called Tonbrux by others).

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In 1286, a blood-coloured star with a long tail was seen towards the cold quarter for three nights.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: In the year of grace 1289, the Kiarend forgot its bed and wandered over Tonbrux (called Sonobun by others), drowning the sheaves.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 1295 the masons of Draeziatam raised the granary to the glory of heaven.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1296, Queen Kryosk fought the men of Festei at Briagri and was driven back. Nothing else of note.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 1296, the Thatham forgot its bed and wandered over Sonobun, drowning the sheaves.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: Be it remembered that in the year 1298 a green fiery sword hung in the sky over the frozen marshes for three nights.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In 1298, a sickly star with a long tail was seen above the pole for three nights.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1304, stars were seen falling above the sunset like rain. Grain was cheap that year.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 1312, the new bridge over the Breitugask was finished. The abbot fell sick in the winter.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1313. Dikes broken at Rogrouv.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year 1323 of the Reckoning, the sun hid its face at noon and the birds fell silent. Wolves were seen near Akrol.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1324, there was a great dearth of bread in Pexiarwyth.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1325, King Drenoum died and was buried at Heidomask (called Pysahiax by others).

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 1325, King Drenoum died and was buried at Heidomask. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Deeds of the Kings, written at Keba
text: In the year of grace 1327, the heavens shut their doors over Pexiarwyth and not a drop fell all summer.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1330. Revolt at Tholaevol. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 1331, the wells of Kubryterk ran dry.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1335. Famine in Lipaskthen. Grain dear.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: Year 1335. Famine in Lipaskthen. Grain dear. The chronicler's hand grew weary.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: Year 1341. Great frost. Bostaem frozen.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: Year 1344. Flood on the Kiarend. Tonbrux (called Sonobun by others) under water.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 1354, the granaries of Steiork stood empty. The old well was cleaned.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Rogrouv
text: 1358. Bridge over the Nougreind finished. Wolves were seen near Ougux.

chronicler: the Chronicle of Draeziatam
text: In the year 1358, the new bridge over the Breitugask was finished.

chronicler: the Town Book of Draeziatam
text: In 1358, stars were seen falling towards the cold quarter like rain.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: Year 1360. Kiarend over its banks. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Day-Book of the house of Rogrouv
text: 1362. Thaebrouth over its banks.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 1362, a blood-coloured comet appeared towards the desert quarter and stayed two nights.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 1365, there was a great dearth of bread in Pexiarwyth. There was hunger for war among the young lords.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 1369, there was a rising in Steiork over the new tax.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In the year 1398, a cloud of sickly grasshoppers settled on Pexiarwyth.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1404. Pestilence at Pysahiax (called Heidomask by others).

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: In 1404, the waters of the Bostaem rose higher than any could remember and covered Pexiarwyth.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: Year 1405. Pilgrims at Tholaevol.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: Year 1411. Grasshoppers, earthen, Tonbrux.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1414. Queen Iapouv married. The tail of the procession stretched to the river.

chronicler: the Book of the Merchants of Lipaskthen
text: 1418. Fire at Lipaskthen. Many said it was an omen.

chronicler: the Town Book of Keba
text: That year, 1418, a great fire broke out in Kubryterk (called Lipaskthen by others) and the granary was lost.
